paragraphs: Azavar works with local governments on the money they are owed. Its focus runs from sales and hospitality taxes to business and franchise fees and disaster relief grants. The software side is Localgov, an online tax and fee administration platform for taxpayers and businesses.

Rather than coming into an office with a paper check, filers submit electronic payments through the platform. Alongside the software, the firm runs revenue reviews covering utility taxes, cable franchise fees, sales taxes, telecom taxes, hotel-motel taxes, and short-term rental taxes. Those reviews run on a contingency fee model, which the company says carries no up-front cost for municipalities. It also produces five-year revenue forecasts so departments do not miss their revenue targets. Staff help communities review, implement, and refine legislation as market conditions change.

Jason Perry founded Azavar in 1996. A technologist by training, he is described as the son of a midwestern city manager. The company added a full revenue-analysis arm in 2006 and a tax remittance and licensing platform in 2016. It says it has served local governments for more than 30 years.

quote.text: when it comes to your community’s money, it never hurts to check.
